_about: Public wording for /arc, one entry per row of docs/qa/parity-audit.md's Feature inventory. scripts/arc-parity.mjs takes each row's status from the ledger and this file's words. arc: the feature in Arc's words. where: where it is in Airc. note: one honest line (needed for Partly and Won't do). since: the first release with it as described. status: only for owner-gated rows, which the ledger can't map (works or partly).

W01.arc: Arc's look: the sidebar and the page as a card

W02.arc: Resize or hide the sidebar, and show it from the edge
W02.where: Drag the sidebar's edge; ⌘S hides it; rest on the window's edge to bring it back

W03.arc: Hold Option to peek at a hidden sidebar
W03.where: Hold ⌥; turn it off in Settings → Appearance

W04.arc: Back, forward and reload in the sidebar
W04.where: Top of the sidebar; right-click or long-press Back for history, ⌘-click for a background tab

W05.note: The sidebar, traffic lights and the Esc exit work as in Arc; some full-screen cases on a second display or with a notch are still being checked.

W06.arc: Show Toolbar: a full address bar over the page

W07.arc: Drag the window by its edges, and a sidebar that dims when Arc is in the background
W07.where: Any empty margin; Settings → Appearance for dragging from the top of a page

W08.note: ⌘T opens on the next frame and the sidebar moves on Arc's springs; typing in ⌘T doesn't always draw on the very next frame yet.

W09.arc: Several windows sharing your Spaces and tabs

W10.arc: Drag a tab out into its own window
W10.where: Drag a tab from the sidebar onto the desktop

S01.arc: Favorites at the top of the sidebar
S01.where: Drag a tab up, or ⌘D… › Add to Favorites; one set per profile, up to twelve

S02.arc: Favorites go back to where they started
S02.where: Click a Favorite; closing one keeps its tile

S03.arc: Unread badges, sound badges and custom icons
S03.where: Right-click a tab or Favorite › Change Icon… / Show Unread Badge

S04.arc: Previews of Gmail, Outlook, calendars, Notion, Linear and Figma
S04.where: Rest the pointer on a pinned tab or Favorite of that site
S04.note: Mail, calendar and recent-page cards work; Notion Calendar has no card, and calendar text is read in English only.

S05.note: Arc retired these in 2024 in favour of Live Folders, which Airc has.

S06.arc: Pinned tabs that remember where they started
S06.where: Pin a tab (⌘D); its address drifts as you browse and comes back when you reset it

S07.arc: Today's tabs: newest on top, and Clear
S07.where: The Today list under your pinned tabs; Clear above it

S08.where: Settings → Profiles › Archive tabs after; playing tabs stay

S09.arc: The tab menu: Share, Change Icon, Customize Page, Move To, Mute, Archive Tabs Below

S10.where: Space menu › New Folder, or drag tabs onto each other

S11.arc: Folder commands: expand all, collapse all, copy links as Markdown

S13.arc: Drag tabs between Spaces and profiles
S13.where: Drag to the sidebar's edge to move to the next Space; hold ⌥ to copy

S14.arc: Drop files, folders and text on the sidebar
S14.where: Drag from the Finder, or + › Add Files…

S15.note: Works for public repositories, or with a GitHub token; Sign in with GitHub isn't available yet.

S16.where: Rest the pointer on a tab in the sidebar

P01.arc: Spaces: name, icon, colour and profile
P01.where: + › New Space…; Manage Spaces… to reorder and rename

P02.where: Click the Space's name, or Tabs › Collapse Pinned Section

P03.arc: Switch Spaces by swiping, keys or clicking
P03.where: Two-finger swipe, ⌃1–⌃9, or the icons at the bottom of the sidebar

P04.arc: Profiles: separate logins, history and extensions per Space

P05.arc: New profiles, signed in to Google, with suggested Favorites
P05.where: Edit a Space › Profile › New Profile…

P06.arc: Space colours: up to three, grain, light or dark

P07.arc: Pages that use your Space's colours (--arc-palette)

P08.arc: Reset all tabs in this Space

C01.arc: Command Bar: search, sites, tabs, Spaces and actions

C03.where: ⌘T, a site's name or shortcut, then Tab; Settings → Site Search

C04.arc: Every menu command in the Command Bar

C05.arc: Copy URL, and copy it as Markdown or a quote

C06.where: ⌘C on selected text; Share Quote under the address
C06.note: Clean links and quote links work; Arc's per-site opt-outs aren't built.

C07.arc: Paste a link into a new tab

C08.note: Nine engines plus your own sites; suggestions come only from the built-in engines, not from imported ones.

V01.arc: Peek: links open in a card over the page
V01.where: Click a link to another site from a pinned tab, or ⇧-click any link; ⌘O makes it a tab

V03.where: Right-click a link › Open Link in Space

V04.arc: Little Arc for links from other apps
V04.where: Make Airc your default browser; ⌘O moves the page into a Space

V05.arc: Little Arc over the app you're in, even in full screen
V05.where: Click a link in any app

V06.arc: Little Arc from anywhere, and show or close them all
V06.where: ⌥⌘N in any app (turn it on in Settings → Links); Window › Show Little Airc Windows

V07.arc: Split View: up to four pages

V08.where: Pin a split, or drag it to Favorites

V09.arc: Expand Current Split and Separate Page from Split View
V09.where: View menu, or a pane's handle

L01.arc: Archive: search, restore and Clear Archive

L02.arc: Archive filters by Space and Little Arc
L02.where: Library › Archive, the filter above the list

L04.arc: Library Media and recent files on hover
L04.where: Library › Media; rest the pointer on the Library button
L04.note: Media and recent files work; Arc's badge on the Library button and Cancel for downloads in progress aren't built.

L05.arc: Notes and Easels in the Library
L05.note: Search, open and export work; Easels have no thumbnail you choose by hand, and deleting moves to the Trash rather than deleting for good.

L07.where: A Space's menu › Export Space…; File › Export All Spaces…

N01.arc: Capture part of a page or one element

N02.arc: Capture Full Page and Portrait Mode
N02.note: Both work; on Safari-engine pages, a very long page's fixed footer can sit slightly off.

N03.where: Capture to an Easel, then refresh it from its page

N05.arc: New Note in Split, and export
N05.where: File › New Note in Split; a note's menu › Export Note…

N06.arc: Share notes by link, and sync them
N06.note: Pinned notes sync through iCloud, tested on one Mac so far; sharing a note by link isn't built yet.

N07.arc: Easels: text, pictures, shapes, arrows and links on a canvas
N07.note: No pencil or freehand drawing, and Easels don't sync between Macs yet.

N08.where: File › Share Easel…, File › Export Easel…
N08.note: Export and read-only links work; editing an Easel together with others isn't available.

B01.arc: Boosts: colours, fonts, Zap, and your own CSS and JavaScript

B05.note: Arc retired it in October 2024; today's Boost editor replaces it.

M01.where: Bottom of the sidebar while something plays in another tab

M02.where: Your keyboard's media keys, Control Centre

M03.arc: Picture in picture for videos, and the Mini Player
M03.note: Works on Chromium pages; on Safari-engine sites (Netflix, Spotify) video uses the Mac's own picture in picture.

M04.arc: Calls float when you leave their tab
M04.note: Tested with simulated calls; not yet with real Meet or Zoom calls.

M05.arc: Call chat and Share This Tab Instead
M05.note: Built for Google Meet; not yet checked on real calls.

M06.arc: Netflix, Spotify, Disney+ and other protected streaming
M06.where: Opens with Safari's engine inside Airc
M06.note: Plays through Safari's engine, so those tabs don't run Chrome extensions; checked signed out only.

M07.note: Finds Chromecast and Google TV; not yet tested with a real TV.

M08.arc: Live Calendar: countdown and Join on a Calendar Favorite
M08.where: Settings → General; right-click the Calendar Favorite for options
M08.note: Reads your Mac's Calendar app and the calendar page itself; it doesn't sign in to Google or Outlook directly.

A01.note: Needs Apple Intelligence (macOS 26); off by default.

A03.where: Settings → AI, then hold ⇧ over a link

A04.where: Library › Downloads; Settings → AI › Rename automatically

A05.note: Airc's AI runs on Apple's on-device model, so it needs Apple Intelligence; nothing goes to an AI service.

A06.where: Tidy in Today, or Tidy Tabs in ⌘T

A07.arc: Ask ChatGPT from the Command Bar
A07.where: ⌘T, type gpt, then Tab (turn on Ask AI in Settings → Site Search)

Y01.note: Spaces, pinned tabs, folders and Favorites sync end-to-end encrypted through iCloud; tested on one Mac so far.

Y02.note: Today tabs, history, logins and Boosts stay on each Mac, and there's no recovery without iCloud Keychain.

Y03.arc: Arc Search on iPhone and Arc for Windows
Y03.note: Airc is a Mac app. It syncs Mac to Mac.

E01.where: The Chrome Web Store; ⌘E lists your extensions

E02.arc: Install an extension in every profile
E02.where: Offered when you install from the Web Store

E03.where: Prompts appear over the page; saved logins in a list under the field
E03.note: Passwords and passkeys saved in Airc work; iCloud Keychain passkeys need Apple's approval first.

E04.arc: Site Controls: permissions, zoom and site data
E04.where: Click the address in the sidebar

E05.where: Settings → Profiles; Site Controls per site
E05.note: On by default with EasyList and EasyPrivacy, and YouTube's player ads are filtered; mid-roll ads, embedded players and ads served by the site itself aren't covered yet.

E06.arc: Developer Tools, View Source and the console

E07.where: Automatic on localhost; ⌃D on any site

E08.arc: Clear Cache and Refresh, Clear Cookies and Refresh, Task Manager
E08.where: View menu; Help › Troubleshooting › Open Task Manager

E09.arc: Save, print, zoom, find and history

E11.arc: Import from Arc and other browsers
E11.note: Spaces, pinned tabs, folders, Favorites, history, logins and cookies come over; some site data (IndexedDB, service workers, session storage) and password notes don't, so a site may ask you to sign in again.

E13.arc: Updates, Restart to Update and release notes
E13.where: New Airc Version Available, above the sidebar's footer

E14.arc: Help: keyboard shortcuts, release notes, feedback

E15.where: Settings → Appearance › App Icon; Settings → General

E16.arc: Arc's own tools: Record Trace, Send to Dia
E16.note: Arc-only plumbing; Airc has its own Send Feedback and data export.

K02.where: Settings → Shortcuts → Sidebar › Include Favorites in ordering

K03.arc: Change any shortcut, and websites first or Arc first

K04.arc: Reveal Current Tab and arrow keys in the sidebar

K05.arc: The Edit menu: spelling, substitutions, speech, Services

K06.note: Goes back through recent tabs within the Space you're in, not across Spaces.

K07.arc: AppleScript and Allow JavaScript from Apple Events
K07.where: View › Developer › Allow JavaScript from Apple Events

Q02.arc: Dark mode, Reduce Motion and contrast

Q03.note: A swipe you reverse halfway doesn't always settle as smoothly as Arc's.

Q04.arc: Paste a Capture into a note

Q05.arc: Fast to start, light on memory
Q05.note: Starts in about a second and unloads idle tabs; a visible page still uses more CPU than in Chrome, and memory with Safari's engine is still being cut down.
